findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add to the selector (549b) an explicit AC that a no-fire candidate is admitted only when C is in some finding's `cohort` set and no finding cites C, a missing-`cohort` row is skipped, and a container/ISF-class criterion is excluded from inline mining — verified by pytest over the four-case synthetic corpus named in the parent AC.
evidence: Parent AC1: 'A no-fire (expect: pass) case for criterion C is emitted only when C is in the cohort set of some finding on that plan AND no finding on that plan cites C; a row with a missing cohort key is skipped ... verified by pytest over a synthetic corpus with an in-cohort silent plan (emitted), a never-in-cohort plan (skipped), a missing-cohort row (skipped), and a container/ISF-class criterion (excluded from inline mining).'

549b Approach: 'Reproduction consensus — the key fired, or stayed absent, consistently across two or more reviews with equal material_fingerprint. The only signal valid in the no-fire direction.' — no mention of cohort membership as an admission precondition.
549b ACs: none reference `cohort`, in-cohort/never-in-cohort/missing-cohort, or container/ISF exclusion; its no-fire AC only asserts 'advisory for one holding reproduction consensus'.
092c non-goal: 'Deciding which candidates qualify ... the selector owns all of that and this child transcribes'.
findings.finding: The parent's no-fire predicate AC is only partially covered: its cohort-based admission rule and its four required sub-cases (in-cohort silent plan emitted, never-in-cohort plan skipped, missing-cohort row skipped, container/ISF-class criterion excluded from inline mining) are not delivered by any sibling's acceptance criteria. The selector (549b) defines the no-fire direction solely via 'reproduction consensus' (a key that stayed absent across equal-fingerprint reviews) and never references the `cohort` routing-proof precondition, the missing-cohort skip, or the container/ISF exclusion in any of its ACs; the emitter (092c) only transcribes.
scenarios: A no-fire fixture is emitted for a plan where C was never routed (missing/absent cohort), encoding non-routing silence as 'finding nothing' — the exact failure the parent predicate exists to prevent.
A container/ISF criterion is mined as an inline no-fire case and cannot be reproduced by the inline finder.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend 549b's ACs (or split the cohort predicate across 549b for admission and 1cef for container/ISF ticketing) so the four-case synthetic-corpus test the parent AC names is owned and measurable.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Assign an owner (likely the self-healing loop 1cef or a new node) for the coverage-reconciliation script that exits non-zero when a routed plan-review criterion is in neither the eval-spec set nor the open `unreliable-criterion:` ticket set, and give it an AC.
evidence: Parent AC2: 'verified by a script that sets the routing key set against ls .rebar/evals/ src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/ and the open-ticket titles, and exits non-zero if any criterion is in neither set.'
1cef ACs cover breaker/ticket creation and gap-only selection but never assert the routing-set-minus-(specs ∪ tickets) is empty.
67aa ACs cover admit/withhold and no-shadowing but not the coverage-completeness reconciliation.
No sibling roster block contains a 'exits non-zero if any criterion is in neither set' verifier.
findings.finding: The parent's coverage AC names a specific verifier — a script that reconciles the routing key set against `ls .rebar/evals/ src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/` and the open `unreliable-criterion:` ticket titles and exits non-zero if any criterion is in neither set — but no sibling's acceptance criteria deliver that union-reconciliation-with-nonzero-exit check. The selector, emitter, admission runner, and self-healing loop each produce pieces (candidates, specs, admitted files, tickets) but none asserts the completion invariant that every routed criterion is in the specs set OR the ticket set.
scenarios: A newly-added criterion is neither mined, admitted, nor ticketed; the epic's coverage AC would pass unnoticed because no child runs the reconciliation script.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC to 1cef (which already knows both the routing set and the ticket set) that runs the reconciliation script and asserts a non-zero exit when any routed criterion is uncovered and unticketed.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Give the container/ISF exclusion + immediate `unreliable-criterion:` (reason: finder not inline-runnable) ticketing an owning AC — in 549b (exclude from candidate list, emit zero-candidate row with reason) and/or 1cef (file the ticket for that reason without the three-run counter).
evidence: Parent Approach: 'Both non-inline classes still carry a cohort tag, so the selector EXCLUDES them from inline mining and the self-healing loop files an unreliable-criterion: ticket (reason: finder not inline-runnable) for each'.
Parent decomposition: 'container/ISF criteria -> the self-healing loop, which files the unreliable-criterion: tickets'.
1cef breaker AC: ticket created only after 'the third consecutive failed run' for reproduction/skipped-unbalanced failures — no path for an immediate not-inline-runnable ticket.
549b ACs: no AC excludes container (G3/G4/decomp-shape) or ISF criteria from the candidate list.
findings.finding: Owned-by-none scope gap: the parent routes container/ISF-class criteria (excluded from inline mining) to the self-healing loop 'which files the unreliable-criterion: ticket (reason: finder not inline-runnable) for each', but no child's acceptance criteria cover this path. The self-healing loop (1cef) creates `unreliable-criterion:` tickets only on the third consecutive failed run (reproduction failure or skipped-unbalanced); it has no AC for a container/ISF criterion whose finder is not inline-runnable, and the selector (549b) has no AC excluding container/ISF criteria from mining.
scenarios: A container criterion (e.g. G3/G4) is routed by effective_routing, is never mined (correctly), but no ticket is ever filed because it never accumulates three failed inline runs — so it lands in neither the eval set nor the ticket set, silently failing the coverage invariant.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 549b AC that a container/ISF-class criterion produces a zero-candidate row with reason 'finder not inline-runnable', and a 1cef AC that such a reason files the `unreliable-criterion:` ticket directly rather than waiting for three failed inline runs.

findings.checklist_item: State the fire-case admission reproduction rule symmetrically with the no-fire branch — e.g. require k-of-n consensus (or a fixed seed / temperature-0 execution) for a FIRE candidate to be admitted, and define how a below-consensus fire candidate is dispositioned (withheld vs unreliable-criterion ticket).
evidence: Plan states no-fire consensus explicitly but is silent on fire-case sampling variance: 'No-fire reproduction consensus ranges over the equal-material_fingerprint reviews meeting this predicate'
evals/eval_solver.py:139-142 runs a real pass1_chunk LLM finder for inline cases (non-deterministic)
evals/eval.py:465-481 executes each case once and scores observed vs expected fire/no-fire — no repeat/consensus for fire cases
Same finder re-runs at change-triggered execution time (AC4), so a flaky admitted fixture becomes a flaky regression gate
findings.finding: The admission runner's 'reproduce against current code' gate for FIRE cases (expect: finding/fail) is under-specified against LLM nondeterminism: the Pass-1 finder is a live model call executed once per case (evals/eval.py scores a single observed fire/no-fire), yet the plan specifies a reproduction-consensus mechanism ONLY for the no-fire branch ('No-fire reproduction consensus ranges over the equal-material_fingerprint reviews'). A single stochastic replay can withhold a genuinely-catching fixture (the finder simply didn't fire that run) or admit one that only intermittently reproduces.
findings.location: Approach — 'admit a fixture only after it reproduces against current code'; Acceptance Criteria bullet 3 ('No fixture enters .rebar/evals/ without having reproduced against current code')
scenarios: A criterion whose historical fire is a borderline/probabilistic finding fails to reproduce on the single admission replay and is wrongly withheld (or filed as unreliable-criterion) despite the rubric being intact
An admitted fire fixture reproduces at admission but flakes on a later rubric-change-triggered run, producing a spurious regression signal
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the admission predicate: a fire candidate is admitted only if it fires in >= m of n replays (mirroring the no-fire consensus over equal-material_fingerprint reviews), and record sub-consensus fire candidates in the drift report as withheld-with-reason rather than hard-failing; document the same replay count for the change-triggered execution path so the gate is stable.

findings.checklist_item: Specify the fire-side (`expect: fail`) selection/consensus rule symmetric to the no-fire predicate: define how a criterion that fired on only a subset of equal-`material_fingerprint` reviews of the same plan is resolved (emit / drop / route to unreliable-criterion) and who owns it.
evidence: The plan specifies only the no-fire side: 'No-fire reproduction consensus ranges over the equal-`material_fingerprint` reviews meeting this predicate; the selector owns it, the emitter transcribes it.'

The emitter is tasked to transcribe 'no-fire candidates to `expect: pass`', but the symmetric decision rule for fire candidates (which fired, how consensus over disagreeing equal-fingerprint reviews yields one `expect: fail` case) is absent — a decision rule referenced by the selector/emitter but not co-located with its inputs (T8 probe b).
AC1 verifies the no-fire predicate over a synthetic corpus but names no fire-disagreement scenario.
findings.finding: The fire-side (`expect: fail`) reproduction/consensus rule is unspecified: the plan defines how NO-FIRE evidence is consolidated across equal-`material_fingerprint` reviews but never states how a criterion that FIRED on only some of several equal-fingerprint reviews of the same plan is resolved into a single `expect: fail` fixture verdict.
findings.location: Approach section, 'No-fire evidence predicate' paragraph and Child decomposition ('selector -> emitter')
scenarios: A plan reviewed 3 times at the same material_fingerprint: criterion C fires in 1 review, is silent (and in-cohort) in 2. The no-fire predicate would admit it as `expect: pass`, yet a finding cites C — contradictory evidence with no stated tie-break.
The emitter receives fire candidates for the same plan where C fired inconsistently and has no rule for whether to emit an `expect: fail` case, drop it, or file an unreliable-criterion ticket.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 'Fire evidence predicate' paragraph mirroring the no-fire one: admit C as `expect: fail` for a plan only when C is cited by findings across a stated majority/consensus of the equal-`material_fingerprint` reviews AND is never silent-in-cohort on any of them; when the equal-fingerprint reviews disagree on whether C fired, route to the self-healing loop as an `unreliable-criterion:` candidate rather than emitting a contradictory case.
